Every REQ the document introduces joins .design/reqs/registry.toml with its evidence, and the generated status view is regenerated rather than hand-edited. Status is DERIVED, never declared — that is the whole argument of RFC-2 and the reason a stale generated table is an error rather than a nit. Adding requirements also drifts the design doc that governs the registry, so doc-drift needs re-pinning in the same pass.

```day-atom
{"in":["design-doc"],"out":["registered-requirements"],"next":["implement"]}
```
